M25_REV_001.source_case_title: TEJ PRAKASH PATHAK & ORS. versus RAJASTHAN HIGH COURT & ORS.
M25_REV_001.claim_text: The rules of the game must not be changed during the course of the game or after the game is played.
M25_REV_001.doctrinal_rationale: Service Law doctrine: 'Rules of the game cannot be changed midstream after the selection process has commenced.' Established in K. Manjusree (2008) and examined by 5-Judge Constitution Bench in Tej Prakash Pathak (2024).

M25_REV_002.source_case_title: SUKANYA SHANTHA versus UNION OF INDIA & ORS.
M25_REV_002.claim_text: Caste-based division of labour and segregation of prisoners in prisons in India violates the Constitution of India.
M25_REV_002.doctrinal_rationale: Constitution of India, Articles 14, 15, 17, 21, and 23: Prohibition of discrimination based on caste, untouchability, right to dignity, and prohibition of forced labour in prison administration.

M25_REV_003.source_case_title: V. SENTHIL BALAJI versus THE DEPUTY DIRECTOR, DIRECTORATE OF ENFORCEMENT
M25_REV_003.claim_text: Prolonged incarceration before being pronounced guilty of an offence should not be permitted to become punishment without trial under Article 21.
M25_REV_003.doctrinal_rationale: Constitution of India, Article 21 & Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973: Fundamental right to speedy trial and protection against prolonged incarceration without trial becoming de facto punishment.

M25_REV_004.source_case_title: TINKU versus STATE OF HARYANA & ORS.
M25_REV_004.claim_text: Compassionate appointment is an exception to the general rule and cannot be claimed as a vested right for appointment.
M25_REV_004.doctrinal_rationale: Service Law & Compassionate Appointment Rules: Articles 14 and 16 equal opportunity in public employment versus humanitarian exceptions for families of deceased breadwinners.

M25_REV_005.source_case_title: IDBI BANK LTD. versus RAMSWAROOP DALIYA AND ORS.
M25_REV_005.claim_text: The auction purchaser may deposit the balance consideration after 15 days without seeking any written consent.
M25_REV_005.doctrinal_rationale: Security Interest (Enforcement) Rules, 2002 under SARFAESI Act, 2002: Rule 9(4) & (5) prescribing 15-day timeline for balance deposit, extendable only with mutual consent in writing.

M25_REV_006.claim_text: The Magistrate may alter an interim maintenance order whenever requested by the husband.
M25_REV_006.doctrinal_rationale: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (DV Act): Sections 12 and 19 concerning residential rights and monetary relief prerequisites.

M25_REV_007.source_case_title: THE STATE OF PUNJAB  versus PARTAP SINGH VERKA
M25_REV_007.claim_text: A public servant can be summoned under Section 319 CrPC to face trial for offences under the PC Act.
M25_REV_007.doctrinal_rationale: Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988: Section 19 mandating prior sanction of competent authority as an indispensable condition precedent for taking cognizance.

M25_REV_008.source_case_title: PRADEEP KUMAR versus THE STATE OF U.P.
M25_REV_008.claim_text: Under Order XXI Rule 99 CPC, an application complaining of dispossession can be made by the judgment debtor.
M25_REV_008.doctrinal_rationale: Statutory Interpretation of Exclusionary Clauses: Legal effect of legislative phrases such as 'other than [specified entity]' or 'excluding [specified class]'.

M25_REV_009.source_case_title: NAEEM versus STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH
M25_REV_009.claim_text: The maritime underwriter is discharged from liability where the cargo vessel was unseaworthy at inception of the voyage.
M25_REV_009.doctrinal_rationale: Marine Insurance Act, 1963: Principles of utmost good faith (uberrima fides) and disclosure of material facts in marine insurance policies.

M25_REV_010.claim_text: Multiplier method based on monthly income and disability percentage must be applied to calculate motor accident compensation.
M25_REV_010.doctrinal_rationale: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988: Sections 166 and 168 regarding just compensation calculation for dependents of deceased accident victims.

M25_REV_011.source_case_title: TINKU versus STATE OF HARYANA & ORS.
M25_REV_011.claim_text: Prior environmental clearance under the EIA Notification mandates conducted public consultation in the affected local area.
M25_REV_011.doctrinal_rationale: Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 & EIA Notification 2006: Statutory requirements for Prior Environmental Clearance before commencement of mining operations.

M25_REV_012.source_case_title: TEJ PRAKASH PATHAK & ORS. versus RAJASTHAN HIGH COURT & ORS.
M25_REV_012.claim_text: The recruiting authority is empowered to alter qualification criteria midway during the selection process.
M25_REV_012.doctrinal_rationale: Service Law Selection Rules: Polarity check testing whether recruitment authority has unilateral authority to relax criteria during ongoing selection.

M25_REV_013.source_case_title: NORTH DELHI MUNICIPAL CORPORATION  versus M/S S.A. BUILDERS LTD.
M25_REV_013.claim_text: The Court may modify an arbitral award under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act.
M25_REV_013.doctrinal_rationale: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996: Section 34 setting aside grounds versus judicial modification of arbitral awards (NHAI v. M. Hakeem doctrine).

M25_REV_014.source_case_title: SUKANYA SHANTHA versus UNION OF INDIA & ORS.
M25_REV_014.claim_text: The Supreme Court held that Parliament has unlimited amending power and Kesavananda is overruled.
M25_REV_014.doctrinal_rationale: Constitutional Law: Basic Structure Doctrine established in Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) and limits on constitutional amending power under Article 368.

M25_REV_015.claim_text: The Patents Act permits unconditional patenting of all agricultural seeds.
M25_REV_015.doctrinal_rationale: Patents Act, 1970: Section 3(j) excluding plants, animals, seeds, and essentially biological processes from patentability in India.

M25_REV_016.source_case_title: V. SENTHIL BALAJI versus THE DEPUTY DIRECTOR, DIRECTORATE OF ENFORCEMENT
M25_REV_016.claim_text: An accused under PMLA is unconditionally entitled to bail upon serving 12 months in custody.
M25_REV_016.doctrinal_rationale: Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (PMLA): Section 45(1) twin conditions for grant of bail and judicial exceptions when trial is indefinitely delayed.

M25_REV_017.source_case_title: SHAJAN SKARIA versus THE STATE OF KERALA AND ANR.
M25_REV_017.claim_text: Anticipatory bail can be granted in offences under the SC/ST Act without examining whether a prima facie case is made out.
M25_REV_017.doctrinal_rationale: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC): Section 100 jurisdiction of High Court in second appeals, strictly confined to substantial questions of law.

M25_REV_018.source_case_title: NAJRUL SEIKH versus DR. SUMIT BANERJEE & ANR.
M25_REV_018.claim_text: A consumer forum must decide medical negligence cases based on the report of the Medical Council.
M25_REV_018.doctrinal_rationale: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996: Section 34(3) proviso establishing a strict 30-day outer limit for condonation of delay, excluding Section 5 Limitation Act.

M25_REV_019.claim_text: The Supreme Court held that Section 34 of the Arbitration Act allows the court to modify an arbitral award.
M25_REV_019.doctrinal_rationale: Arbitration Law & Source Role: Distinction between counsel's argument seeking award modification and the court's definitive ratio holding modification impermissible.

M25_REV_020.claim_text: The Supreme Court ruled that executive remission decisions are completely immune from judicial review.
M25_REV_020.doctrinal_rationale: Criminal Procedure & Source Role: Distinction between State counsel's submission on remission policy and the court's constitutional interpretation under Article 161.

M25_REV_021.claim_text: The Supreme Court ruled that banks have absolute right to forfeit earnest money without affording any hearing.
M25_REV_021.doctrinal_rationale: SARFAESI Law & Source Role: Distinction between secured creditor's argument advocating automatic forfeiture and the court's equitable interpretation of Rule 9.

M25_REV_022.claim_text: The 2024 bench adopted its own binding ruling that registration of FIR is mandatory under Section 154 CrPC upon disclosing cognizable offence.
M25_REV_022.doctrinal_rationale: Criminal Procedure & Quoted Precedents: Distinguishing Lalita Kumari (2014) mandatory FIR principles from the instant bench's operative ratio.

M25_REV_023.claim_text: The 2024 bench adopted as its own ruling the requirement to prepare arrest memos and notify relatives.
M25_REV_023.doctrinal_rationale: Constitutional Safeguards & Quoted Precedents: Distinguishing D.K. Basu (1997) arrest guidelines cited in passing from the instant judgment's holding.

M25_REV_024.claim_text: The 2024 bench adopted its own binding ruling that procedure established by law must be just, fair, and reasonable.
M25_REV_024.doctrinal_rationale: Constitutional Law & Quoted Precedents: Distinguishing Maneka Gandhi (1978) Article 21 natural justice doctrine cited in submissions from the holding.

M25_REV_025.source_case_title: V. SENTHIL BALAJI versus THE DEPUTY DIRECTOR, DIRECTORATE OF ENFORCEMENT
M25_REV_025.claim_text: The Supreme Court held that prolonged incarceration without trial violates Article 21 and ruled that all undertrial prisoners are entitled to immediate discharge.
M25_REV_025.doctrinal_rationale: Criminal Jurisprudence: Testing whether constitutional finding on delay overgeneralizes into an automatic rule of discharge in all pending trials.

M25_REV_026.source_case_title: SUKANYA SHANTHA versus UNION OF INDIA & ORS.
M25_REV_026.claim_text: The Court held that caste-based labor segregation in prisons violates Article 14 and ruled that all existing prison convictions stand quashed.
M25_REV_026.doctrinal_rationale: Prison Reforms: Testing whether judicial declaration of unconstitutionality of caste segregation invalidates all operational prison rules universally.

M25_REV_027.source_case_title: TEJ PRAKASH PATHAK & ORS. versus RAJASTHAN HIGH COURT & ORS.
M25_REV_027.claim_text: The Court held that the rules of the game cannot be changed midway and ruled that every candidate in the written test is mandatorily entitled to appointment.
M25_REV_027.doctrinal_rationale: Service Law: Testing whether empanelment in a select list overgeneralizes into an indefeasible legal right to appointment.

M25_REV_028.claim_text: The Supreme Court ruled under Article 142 that all educational fee deadlines are universally forgiven.
M25_REV_028.doctrinal_rationale: Higher Education Admissions: Ambiguity regarding exercise of Article 142 extraordinary equitable jurisdiction versus general statutory deadlines.

M25_REV_029.claim_text: The Court held that every commercial building automatically qualifies as plant under Section 17(5)(d).
M25_REV_029.doctrinal_rationale: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017: Section 17(5)(d) exception for 'plant' and the application of the functionality test to commercial buildings.

M25_REV_030.claim_text: The remedies under the Consumer Protection Act and the Arbitration Act operate concurrently without mutual exclusion.
M25_REV_030.doctrinal_rationale: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 vs Arbitration Act: Doctrine of election and non-exclusion of consumer remedies by commercial arbitration clauses.
